text:
nina: FYI spotted a regression in header parsing causing 502s for a small % of eu-edge embedding calls. PR 4892 fixes it. Low-risk but customer-facing. Can we expedite a hotfix to eu-edge? :pray:
release_mgr: please paste PR link + brief rollback plan. We'll need ops + oncall signoff for expedited deploy.
nina: https://github.com/redwood-inference/repo/pull/4892 - single-line change in header sanitizer. Rollback = revert to image redwood-main-2026-04-01, ~3-5m. No DB changes.
sre_lead: Can we run a short canary (5% for 10m) and watch error-rate & latency? Also pin the image tag during rollout.
ops-rotation: oncall checked stack traces, matches header parser. +1 for expedite once canary is healthy.
ci-bot: CI passed: unit tests 142/142, integration smokers ok. Build image: image:redwood-hotfix-4892 available.
release_mgr: tagging image and preparing canary. Will set canary=5% timeout=10m. Need explicit /deploy command.
releasebot: To deploy run: `./deploy/deploy.sh --env eu-edge --image redwood-hotfix-4892 --canary 5% --timeout 10m`
release_mgr: running now. output: ```
> ./deploy/deploy.sh --env eu-edge --image redwood-hotfix-4892 --canary 5% --timeout 10m
deploybot: started job 9922 creating canary slice (5%)```
deploybot: canary pods up (3 small instances in eu-west1), healthchecks ok, tailing errors: reduced in canary group.
sre_lead: Observability: 10m window looks good. No CPU/mem regression. p95 latency unchanged. Recommend promote.
release_mgr: promoting to 100% -> `./deploy/promote.sh --job 9922 --to 100%`
deploybot: promotion underway, old pods draining, new image rolled to all eu-edge nodes.
releasebot: deploy finished. All eu-edge on redwood-hotfix-4892. Post-deploy: error-rate back to baseline, no new alerts.
nina: thanks team. I'll backport the fix to the 2026-03 maintenance branch and add release notes. :tada:
ops-rotation: keeping watch for 30m and will update runbook if needed.
release_mgr: marking ticket #1184 as expedited hotfix deployed. Rollback command recorded in ticket. Closing thread.
